chapterNotes: Chapter 4 theme: the wild lands strike back. Each level leans on a primitive chapter 3 could not use, built in S4 L7-E: stage timed raids and hazards (a trigger with `after` an objective index starts its clock when that stage is done), wolf packs that arrive by trigger (a `spawn` of a beast unit with tribe -1 makes a new den), neutral hazards (a `spell` reward on a trigger with a casting `tribe` of -1: eruptions, quakes, storms, fire rain, mire, which hurt every tribe), and three or four tribe maps with `kill` objectives naming one tribe (the level bot ranks that tribe first). The level bot cannot cast spells from scripts and must always have a way to win: keep a land route, causeway or Boathouse open, and never let a hazard make a goal impossible. A hazard should land where it changes a decision (a stone, a road, a landing), and every repeating hazard or raid has a warning message about 10 s before and is bounded by `until`. Keep rivals alive until their stage with data (maxPopulation, posted home guards, a fortified Hearth) so destroy and eliminate goals cannot finish early. Chapter 4 ramps from about 16000 at level 36 to about 38500 at level 45; each level should finish later than the one before it.

briefs.name: Smoke on the Wind
briefs.brief: Opens chapter 4. A green valley with a smoking volcano (map paint cone) on its eastern side; the player starts in the west with a small village, a small sneaky rival lives beyond the cone in the east. Once the first stage is done the mountain erupts on its own: a repeating trigger (after the first objective) casts Volcano as tribe -1 on the cone's western flank every 120 to 150 s, with a warning message before each. A ley stone sits on that flank inside the eruption reach, so taking and keeping it means timing the eruptions. Stages: grow to about 25 followers; take the ley stone on the flank; raise two Watchtowers facing the pass around the cone; destroy the rival Hearth. Give the player Raise Land and one attacking spell. Teach in the messages that the mountain hurts everyone, rivals included.

briefs.name: The Howling Woods
briefs.brief: A wooded upland. The player's village sits in a clearing in the south; a turtle rival holds a walled hill in the north behind the woods. Wolves come in waves as the player pushes in: each finished stage wakes a new pack (a trigger with after that spawns wolves with tribe -1 at a named clearing, which makes a new den). Stages: clear the den by the village (clearDens with at and r); worship at the old shrine in the deep woods with followers while a new pack is spawned near it; clear the two dens that woke around the shrine; train and kill about 10 of the rival's troops (kill with tribe 1); then destroy the rival's lodge or Hearth. Use props (fallen logs, cairns, standing stones) to make the shrine glade read.

briefs.name: Caught Between
briefs.brief: The first three tribe map of the chapter. The player sits in the middle of a broad river valley between an aggressive rival to the east (tribe 1) and a sneaky raiding tribe to the west (tribe 2); the two rivals also fight each other. After the first stage, tribe 2 sends fresh raiding bands at the player on a stage timed trigger (after, raid fresh, every 150 to 200 s, until the kill stage is done). Stages: grow and raise a Warden Lodge; kill about 12 of tribe 2's troops (kill with tribe 2, the raiders); take the seer stone on the island in the river between the rivals; destroy tribe 2's Hearth; destroy tribe 1's Hearth. Keep tribe 1 alive (maxPopulation, posted guards) until its stage.

briefs.name: The Shaking Plain
briefs.brief: A low coastal plain only a little above the sea, crossed by an old raised road (a ridge or rect paint just above the plain) from the player's village in the south west to a rival (aggressive) on a rocky rise in the north east. After the first stage the ground starts to shake: a repeating trigger casts Quake as tribe -1 at points on the plain beside the road every 120 to 150 s (warning first), so the sea creeps into the low ground but the raised road always survives (place the quakes so the road and the bot's route stay open). Two stones stand on low knolls beside the road (a ward and a ley). Stages: grow to about 30 followers; take both stones; hold both at once for about 120 s while quakes and rival bands contest them; destroy the rival Hearth. Give the player Raise Land and Flatten so a human can repair the plain.

briefs.name: Storm Coast
briefs.brief: An archipelago. The player has a home isle; a seer stone stands on a small outer isle; the rival (turtle, tribe 1) holds the far isle; a raiding tribe (tribe 2, aggressive, small, maxPopulation capped) lives on a rocky isle and lands bands on the player's shore by stage timed raids. Storms sweep the sea lane between the home isle and the outer isle: a repeating trigger casts Whirlwind or Lightning as tribe -1 over the lane every 120 to 160 s once the Boathouse stage is done (warning first). Stages: raise a Boathouse (the level bot now raises a requested Boathouse at once); ferry followers to the outer isle and take the seer; kill about 10 of tribe 2's landing raiders (kill with tribe 2); destroy tribe 1's Hearth on the far isle. A human should feel the storm timing when ferrying.

briefs.name: The Pack Mother
briefs.brief: Deep wolf country under a hill crowned with a moon stone. The player and a sneaky rival start on opposite sides of a forest full of dens, and the wolves hunt both tribes. Stages: clear the dens nearest the village; worship at the moon stone on the hill (a worship site with a useful reward); that wakes the pack mother: a trigger with after spawns a large pack (tribe -1, a new den) on the road between the player and the rival, plus two smaller packs later on a stage timer; clear the great den; survive the rival's night raids for a few minutes (survive fromStage, with stage timed raids bounded by until); destroy the rival Hearth. Use beastPrey only if the design needs the wolves to ignore the rival.

briefs.name: Four Hearths
briefs.brief: A four tribe map: the player in the south, an aggressive tribe in the west (tribe 1), a turtle tribe in the north (tribe 2) and a sneaky raiding tribe in the east (tribe 3), all hostile to each other, around a central ley crown of three stones. Cap each rival's population so the map stays bounded. Stages: grow and train; kill about 12 of tribe 3's raiders (kill with tribe 3) while tribe 3 sends stage timed raids; destroy tribe 3's Hearth; take and hold two of the central stones; kill about 10 of tribe 1's troops; destroy tribe 1's and tribe 2's Hearths (or eliminateAll as the last stage once only they remain). The level bot ranks a kill objective's tribe first, so name tribes in kill goals.

briefs.name: The Burning Field
briefs.brief: A wide dry grassland between the player's hills in the west and a fortified aggressive rival in the east, with a reliquary in the middle of the field. Once the player takes the reliquary's ward stone, fire rain starts sweeping the middle of the field: a repeating trigger (after) casts Fire Rain as tribe -1 at points across the field every 120 to 150 s, warning first. A second, smaller tribe (tribe 2, sneaky) lives in the southern hills and sends stage timed raids at the player's worshippers. Stages: raise a Warden Lodge and a Firecaller lodge (two build goals or one build plus followers); take the ward stone in the field; worship at the reliquary through the fire (worship with followers); kill about 12 of tribe 2's troops; destroy the rival Hearth in the east.

briefs.name: The Drowning Mire
briefs.brief: A wide marsh of low isles joined by causeways that drown at high tide (tides like salt_marsh), with wolf dens on two isles and three tribes: the player in the south west, a turtle tribe in the north (tribe 1) and an aggressive tribe in the east (tribe 2). After the second stage the marsh itself turns on everyone: a repeating trigger casts Mire as tribe -1 on the causeway heads every 140 to 180 s (warning first), so crossings must be timed against both the tide and the mire. Stages: raise a Boathouse or cross the first causeway at low tide (reach with a named unit); clear the two dens; take a seer and a ley stone on two isles; hold both for about 150 s; kill about 12 of tribe 2's troops; destroy tribe 1's Hearth. Keep a Boathouse route open so the bot always has a crossing.

briefs.name: The Wild Heart
briefs.brief: The chapter finale. A great volcano (map paint cone, very high) rises at the center of the map with an ancient summit shrine; three rival tribes ring it (aggressive west, sneaky north east, turtle south east), and the player starts in the south west. Every stage wakes more of the wild: stage timed eruptions on the cone (Volcano as tribe -1), a wolf pack spawned by trigger on the slopes, quakes on the lowland roads later on, each with a warning and bounded by until. Stages: grow to about 40 followers; kill about 12 of the sneaky tribe's raiders (kill with its tribe) as its stage timed raids come in; destroy the sneaky tribe's Hearth; take the ley stone on the lower slope; walk the Shaper to the summit and worship at the shrine (shaper only worship, it teaches or grants a strong spell); destroy the aggressive tribe's Hearth; eliminate every remaining tribe (eliminateAll as the last stage). This should be the longest and hardest level so far, but every stage must stay a fight or a decision, never a wait.
